utils.io package#

utils.io.batch_bw_loader module#

Batch BigWig Loader Module

This module provides a class to load data from multiple BigWig files in parallel, keeping file handles open for efficient batch retrieval.

class utils.io.batch_bw_loader.BatchBigWigLoader(bw_paths_df, num_bins, bin_size, n_workers=8)[source]#

Bases: object

A context-managed loader for reading multiple BigWig files in parallel.

This class opens multiple BigWig files during context entry, keeps them open in memory, and uses a ThreadPool to read them concurrently when load_batch is called.

load_batch(coords)[source]#

Loads a batch of intervals for all tracks in parallel.

Parameters:

coords (list of tuple) – List of genomic intervals as [(chrom, start, end), …].

Returns:

A 3D array of shape (batch_size, num_tracks, num_bins) containing the accumulated signals.

Return type:

np.ndarray

utils.io.data_input module#

Data Input and Squashing Module

This module provides functions and classes to scale, squash, and invert predictions/targets for Borzoi and AlphaGenome model architectures.

class utils.io.data_input.SelectiveSquashTransform(rna_task_indices: List[int], task_axis: int = -2, transform: str = 'Borzoi', track_means: numpy.ndarray | torch.Tensor | None = None, inverse: bool = False)[source]#

Bases: object

A callable transform to selectively apply/invert scaling and squashing.

Compatible with PyTorch Lightning DataLoaders and native model transforms. Allows applying Borzoi or AlphaGenome transformations specifically to certain task tracks (e.g. RNA-seq).

Returns:

Scaled and optionally squashed targets.

TensorOrArray

utils.io.data_input.get_non_zero_track_means(preds: numpy.ndarray) → numpy.ndarray[source]#

Calculates the non-zero mean per track for predictions.

Calculates the mean for each track across all intervals and bins, considering only non-zero and non-NaN values. Highly memory efficient.

Parameters:

preds (np.ndarray) – Predictions array of shape (intervals, tracks, bins).

Returns:

A 1D array of shape (tracks,) with non-zero means.

Return type:

np.ndarray

utils.io.data_input.get_streaming_non_zero_track_means(bw_paths_df, intervals_df, bin_size, batch_size=256)[source]#

Computes non-zero track means across all intervals in a streaming fashion.

Iterates through the intervals and loads BigWig data in batches, accumulating sums and counts of non-zero, non-NaN entries to compute the final track means. This avoids loading the entire dataset into RAM.

Parameters:

  • bw_paths_df (pandas.DataFrame) – DataFrame containing a ‘path’ column of BigWig files.

  • intervals_df (pandas.DataFrame) – DataFrame containing ‘chrom’, ‘start’, and ‘end’ columns for the intervals.

  • bin_size (int) – Size of each bin in base pairs.

  • batch_size (int, optional) – Batch size for loading data. Defaults to 256.

Returns:

A 1D array of shape (tracks,) containing the computed non-zero track means.

Return type:

np.ndarray

utils.io.data_output module#

Data Output Module

This module provides helper functions to save predictions to compressed and structured formats (like annotated HDF5), with fallbacks if dependencies like h5py are missing.

utils.io.data_output.save_borzoi_predictions_with_fallback(preds, out_dir, file_prefix, intervals_df=None, tracks_df=None)[source]#

Attempts to save predictions as an annotated HDF5 file; falls back to numpy (.npy) on failure.

This function compiles predictions and optional metadata (interval and track annotations) into a structured HDF5 dataset, with gzip compression. If h5py is not installed or the write fails, it falls back to saving as a plain NumPy .npy file.

Parameters:

  • preds (np.ndarray) – The predictions array to save.

  • out_dir (str or Path) – Output directory where the file will be saved.

  • file_prefix (str) – Prefix name of the output file (excluding extension).

  • intervals_df (pandas.DataFrame, optional) – DataFrame containing annotations for the genomic intervals. Saved as the “intervals” group in HDF5.

  • tracks_df (pandas.DataFrame, optional) – DataFrame containing annotations for the tracks. Saved as the “tracks” group in HDF5.

utils.io.variant_annotation module#

Variant Annotation Module

This module provides functions to annotate a pandas DataFrame of genetic variants (VCF-style) with various genomic features, conservation scores, and coding effects.

Expected Input Data Format:#

The core input to most of these functions is a pandas DataFrame representing genetic variants. At a minimum, this DataFrame must contain the following columns:

  • Chrom or Chromosome (str): The chromosome (e.g., ‘1’, ‘chr1’, ‘X’).

  • Pos (int): The 1-based genomic position of the variant.

  • Ref (str): The reference allele.

  • Alt (str): The alternate allele.

Some downstream functions (like coding effects) rely on the output of upstream functions (like GTF feature annotation), which will be explicitly noted in their respective docstrings.

utils.io.variant_annotation.annotate_cCREs(ccre_pr: pyranges.PyRanges, vcf_pr: pyranges.PyRanges) → pandas.DataFrame[source]#

Annotates variants with ENCODE candidate cis-Regulatory Elements (cCREs).

Performs a left genomic overlap join of variants against the preloaded cCREs.

Parameters:

  • ccre_pr (pr.PyRanges) – Preloaded cCRE features.

  • vcf_pr (pr.PyRanges) – PyRanges containing variant coordinates.

Returns:

A DataFrame of variants annotated with cCRE identifiers and classes.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

utils.io.variant_annotation.annotate_cadd_snv_scores(df: pandas.DataFrame, bw_paths: Dict[str, str]) → pandas.DataFrame[source]#

Extracts CADD PHRED scores for SNVs from allele-specific BigWig files.

Filters out Indels automatically, mapping the remaining single nucleotide variants to their corresponding target allele BigWig track.

Parameters:

  • df (pd.DataFrame) – DataFrame containing ‘Chromosome’, ‘Pos’, ‘Ref’, and ‘Alt’.

  • bw_paths (Dict[str, str]) – Dictionary mapping the alternate alleles to their specific BigWig paths, e.g.: {‘A’: ‘cadd1.7PhredSnvA.bw’, ‘C’: ‘…’}

Returns:

Contains only the filtered SNVs alongside their coordinates,

alleles, and the resulting ‘CADD_PHRED_score’.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

utils.io.variant_annotation.annotate_cardioid_enhancer_overlap(variants_df: pandas.DataFrame, regions_df: pandas.DataFrame) → pandas.DataFrame[source]#

Annotates variants with overlapping cardioid enhancer regions.

Determines which variants fall within the specified enhancer regions, appending their regulatory positions, cell type specificity, and H3K27ac histone modification status. Duplicates are resolved by prioritizing H3K27ac positive overlaps.

Parameters:

  • variants_df (pd.DataFrame) – DataFrame containing genetic variants (must have CHROM and POS).

  • regions_df (pd.DataFrame) – DataFrame containing enhancer regions (must have seqnames, start, and end).

Returns:

DataFrame of overlapping variants annotated with enhancer regulatory position, histone status, and cell types.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

utils.io.variant_annotation.annotate_coding_effect(variants_df: pandas.DataFrame, batch_size: int = 200, sleep: float = 0.5) → pandas.DataFrame[source]#

Queries the Ensembl VEP REST API for coding consequence, amino acid changes, and impact.

Note: This function filters internally to only request VEP data for variants already annotated as coding (CDS, start/stop codon, exon).

Parameters:

  • variants_df (pd.DataFrame) – Must contain ‘Chromosome’, ‘Pos’, ‘Ref’, ‘Alt’, and ‘gtf_feature’.

  • batch_size (int) – Number of variants to query in a single API POST request.

  • sleep (float) – Wait time in seconds between API requests to prevent rate limiting.

Returns:

Contains columns ‘all_effects’, ‘coding_effect’, ‘aa_change’,

and ‘impact’ aligned to the input variants_df index.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

utils.io.variant_annotation.annotate_gtf_features(variants_df: pandas.DataFrame, gtf_df: pandas.DataFrame) → pandas.DataFrame[source]#

Annotates variants with the most specific overlapping GTF feature and calculates absolute distance to the closest Transcription Start Site (TSS).

Hierarchy (most to least specific): start_codon / stop_codon > CDS > UTR > exon > intron > gene

Parameters:

  • variants_df (pd.DataFrame) – Variant dataframe. Must contain ‘Chromosome’, ‘Start’, and ‘End’ columns (0-based coordinates).

  • gtf_df (pd.DataFrame) – GTF dataframe parsed into standard columns (‘chrom’, ‘start’, ‘end’, ‘feature’, ‘strand’, ‘gene_name’, ‘gene_type’).

Returns:

DataFrame aligned with the input index, containing columns:

’gtf_feature’, ‘gene_name’, ‘gene_type’, and ‘closest_TSS’.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

Translates 1-based ‘Pos’ coordinates to 0-based half-open intervals (‘Start’, ‘End’) required by PyRanges.

Module contents#

IO Package#

This package contains modules and classes for reading genomic data, handling scaling/transformations (such as Borzoi and AlphaGenome squash formats), and saving predictions or annotations.

Submodules:#

  • batch_bw_loader: Contains BatchBigWigLoader, a class to load multiple BigWig tracks in parallel.

  • data_input: Contains mathematical squash operations and data loading helpers.

  • data_output: Contains utilities to save predictions into formats like annotated HDF5.

  • variant_annotation: Contains functions to annotate genetic variant dataframes with genomic features.
